title: HyperLoRA factor generation vs client Mirror code
hypothesis: For clients whose rank-2 LoRA updates share a left factor and lie on a sinusoidal task orbit, one shared LoRA basis plus a phase code will reproduce unseen client adapters with lower actual server+client payload than a HyperLoRA-style generator that emits full A/B initialization. A direct low-rank coefficient control and an ordinary scalar phase control determine whether any gain is Mirror-specific. An off-orbit client may require private rank-2 factors.
physical_object: one shared 16x16 base weight, rank-2 left LoRA factor B, and two right-factor basis matrices A1/A2
mirror_coordinate: one phase angle per client selecting cos(theta) A1 + sin(theta) A2
logical_multiplicity: 64 client adapters on a rank-2 orbit, including 16 clients held out from local fitting, plus one off-orbit client
controls: HyperLoRA-style linear generator emitting full client-specific A/B factors from 2D client embeddings
HyperLoRA generator with/without private off-orbit factors
Mirror phase with/without private rank-2 factors
ordinary scalar phase code with identical inference state

development.selection_metric: unseen-client output nMSE, actual total payload bytes, client communication bytes, factor-generation MACs, private-state need

storage.authority: actual deterministic ZIP/NPY FP32 inference payload after reload
paid_objects: HyperLoRA generator or shared B/A basis

success_gate: All fresh seeds: unseen-client nMSE <=1e-5; Mirror total payload at least 20% below HyperLoRA with private fallback; Mirror at least 10% below both direct coefficient and native scalar-phase controls at equal quality; generation compute <=2x HyperLoRA; report communication and off-orbit private state.
failure_gate: Unseen quality misses 1e-5 in at least two fresh seeds; or storage reduction vs HyperLoRA is <20%; or a direct/native control is within 10% bytes at equal quality; or generation compute exceeds 2x.
development_decision: On both development worlds, HyperLoRA full-factor generator with the private fallback had lower serialized bytes than Mirror (2,861B vs 2,980B; 2,874B vs 2,976B). Mirror also missed the 20% payload margin versus HyperLoRA, and the native phase control was byte/hash identical. Since the representation shapes and exact synthetic family are fixed, freeze FAIL at development and keep fresh seeds sealed.
amendment: After development-only inspection and before fresh access, lock the stated development stop. No fresh results were accessed; quality or byte thresholds were not changed. Seeds 34211–34213 remain sealed.
boundaries: synthetic post-fit linear LoRA functions, not neural model fine-tuning
client features are available to both HyperLoRA and Mirror; 16 unseen clients have no local examples
HyperLoRA control is a linear full-factor generator on a planted task manifold, not a reproduction of the full HyperLoRA training stack
no optimizer updates; client adapters are estimated from local linear regression support data and generator fitted by least squares
one off-orbit client is included to measure private rank-2 factor need
